name: Channels
desc: Where a human meets the system

comps.name: EHR-embedded app
comps.purpose: The ordering physician never leaves the chart. A SMART App Launch opens the pre-auth view with patient and encounter context already resolved, and CDS Hooks cards appear at order-select and order-sign.
inputs: SMART launch token with patient + encounter context
outputs: Cards rendered in the chart: authorisation required, documents needed, alternatives
A deep link into the case when the clinician wants detail
comps.prod: Registered as a confidential client with each EHR vendor; scopes negotiated per site.

comps.name: Provider portal
comps.purpose: The web surface the pre-auth coordinator lives in all day. Work queue, packet review, approvals, appeals. This is the screen the live demo shows.
inputs: Agent activity stream over the event bus
outputs: Human approval decisions, edits and overrides — all written to the audit log
protocols: Server-sent events for the activity stream
comps.prod: Role-based access; every approval carries the approver's identity and a timestamp.

comps.name: Payer-side view
comps.purpose: Where a payer's utilisation-management reviewer sees the same packet, the same criteria and the same evidence links the provider saw. Shared context is what removes the phone call.
outputs: Decision, pend reason or additional-information request
comps.prod: In reality this is the payer's own UM system; the prototype shows it to make the round trip legible.

comps.name: Patient notifications
comps.purpose: Tells the patient what is happening without them having to call the office. Status, expected decision date, and their share of cost once the benefit is known.
outputs: SMS / email / patient app message with plain-language status
comps.prod: Consent-gated per channel; language and reading level configurable.

name: Agent orchestration
desc: Specialist agents under one orchestrator, with human checkpoints

comps.name: Orchestrator
comps.purpose: Decides which specialist agent runs next, on what evidence, and when to stop and ask a human. It holds the case plan; the specialists hold no state of their own.
inputs: Case events from the event bus
outputs: The next task, or a human checkpoint
A replayable decision trace for the audit log
comps.prod: Deterministic state machine at the top level; model calls only inside individual agent steps, so a failure is contained to one step and can be retried.

comps.name: Seven specialist agents
comps.purpose: Intake, Eligibility, Clinical Evidence, Policy Matching, Packet Assembly, Submission & Tracking, Denial & Appeal. Each has one job, one set of tools and one escalation rule. See the Agents screen.
inputs: A scoped task from the orchestrator
outputs: A structured result with citations, plus a confidence score
protocols: No direct database access — every read goes through a platform API so it is audited
comps.prod: Each agent is independently testable against recorded cases; a regression suite of real historical determinations is the only honest way to measure them.

comps.name: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints
comps.purpose: The hard gates. Nothing is submitted, no appeal is filed and no clinical assertion is added without a named human approving it. Confidence below threshold routes here automatically.
outputs: Approval, edit or rejection, attributed to a person
protocols: Signed approval record written to the audit log
comps.prod: Configurable thresholds by service line, payer and dollar amount. Clinical assertions always require a clinician, not a coordinator.

comps.name: Agent memory & case state
comps.purpose: Per-case working state, plus cross-case memory: which evidence satisfied which criterion for which payer, which phrasings got pended, which reviewers ask for what.
outputs: Priors that raise first-pass rates over time
Payer-specific packet templates
protocols: Vector + relational store, scoped per payer and per policy
comps.prod: This is the compounding asset. It is also the part that needs the tightest governance — it must never leak one organisation's outcomes into another's.

name: Platform — the Medblocks-equivalent layer
desc: Built first. The workflow is a tenant of it, not a peer.

comps.name: Clinical data repository
comps.purpose: One longitudinal record per patient, reconciled across every connected source. Raw payloads are kept verbatim; the queryable shape is derived. This is what makes 'find the evidence' a query rather than an integration project.
outputs: AQL and FHIR search results with provenance on every element
comps.prod: Keeping raw alongside derived is what lets you re-normalise later without re-pulling a decade of data.

comps.name: Terminology service
comps.purpose: Turns 'the payer asked for a TB screen' into a value set of LOINC codes the repository can actually be searched with, and back again. Without it, criteria matching is string matching.
inputs: Code system lookups, value set expansions, code maps
outputs: Expanded value sets, translated codes, display names
comps.prod: Licensing matters — SNOMED CT and CPT are licensed content. Budget for it before you design around it.

comps.name: Form & template engine
comps.purpose: Renders the payer's questionnaire and autofills every answer the repository already holds, using CQL expressions the payer shipped with the form. The clinician supplies only what the plan genuinely does not know.
inputs: Patient data for the autofill expressions
outputs: QuestionnaireResponse with provenance per answer
comps.prod: The single largest piece of burden reduction in CMS-0057-F, and the piece most often skipped.

comps.name: Rules & policy store
comps.purpose: Payer policies held as structured, versioned criteria rather than PDFs. Each criterion carries the evidence type that satisfies it. Versioned, because a case must be judged against the policy in force on its date.
inputs: Payer policy documents, CRD responses, DTR questionnaires
outputs: Structured criteria a matching agent can reason over, with citations
comps.prod: Getting policies into this shape is the least glamorous and most valuable work in the whole system.

comps.name: Identity & consent
comps.purpose: Resolves the same patient across sources, authenticates every actor including the agents, and records the legal basis for each data access.
outputs: A resolved patient identity, an authorised principal, a permitted purpose
comps.prod: Duplicate patient records are a clinical safety problem, not a data-quality footnote — which is why matching sits here and not at the edge.

comps.name: Audit log
comps.sub: Every read, every agent step, every approval
comps.purpose: An append-only record of who or what touched which record, why, and what they decided. Regulators ask; payers ask; your own clinicians ask. An agent system without this is unshippable.
inputs: Every platform API call, every agent step, every human decision
outputs: Queryable audit trail; a full replay of any case
comps.prod: Agent steps must be logged with the model, the prompt version and the evidence used, or you cannot defend a determination afterwards.

comps.name: Event bus
comps.purpose: Decouples the workflow from the platform. A new lab lands; the bus emits an event; a pended case that was waiting for exactly that lab wakes up on its own.
inputs: Record ingestion, case transitions, payer responses, connection health
outputs: Subscriptions for agents, webhooks for external systems
comps.prod: This is what makes the more-info loop cheap: nobody polls, and nobody has to remember to check.

comps.name: FHIR gateway
comps.purpose: A single FHIR facade in front of every connected source, so the agents never learn a vendor dialect. It also keeps each source's token inside the trust boundary that issued it.
outputs: Normalised resources, with the source recorded
comps.prod: Never forward an EHR's token onward. Proxy the read and re-tokenize — the CRD implementation guide is explicit about this.

comps.name: EHR connectors
comps.purpose: Per-vendor connection lifecycle: registration, token refresh forever, paging through FHIR for years, and telling you when a connection has quietly lapsed.
inputs: Authorisation grants per organisation or per patient
outputs: A live connection, plus events when it breaks
comps.prod: The unglamorous permanent work: refresh tokens, re-consent flows, vendor-specific scope quirks.

comps.name: Payer & clearinghouse connectors
comps.purpose: Three tiers of payer, one interface upward. Full Da Vinci payers get PAS; partial payers get CRD plus X12 278; legacy payers get browser automation and fax, wrapped so the agents cannot tell the difference.
inputs: An approved packet in canonical form
outputs: A submission on whatever transport that payer supports, plus a tracking number
comps.prod: The legacy tier is the one that carries operational risk and is the reason the rule exists. Plan to support it through 2027 and beyond.

comps.name: Document & OCR ingestion
comps.purpose: Turns the scanned outside record into something the evidence agent can search. A large share of the evidence that decides these cases arrives as an image.
outputs: Extracted text and structured findings, linked to the source page
comps.prod: Always keep the page image next to the extraction. A reviewer will want to see the original line.

name: External systems
desc: Not yours. Meet them where they are.

comps.name: Provider EHRs
comps.purpose: Where the order is placed and where the evidence lives. The EHR is both the trigger and the primary source.
inputs: Your registered SMART app and CDS service
outputs: Orders, notes, labs, imaging, coverage on file
comps.prod: Site-by-site registration and scope approval; assume months, not days, for the first one.

comps.name: Payers
comps.purpose: CRD answers whether authorisation is needed; DTR supplies the questionnaire; PAS takes the submission. Most payers will not have all three on day one.
inputs: CRD hook calls, DTR questionnaire fetches, PAS bundles
outputs: Requirement answers, questionnaires, determinations
comps.prod: CMS-0057-F binds covered plans by 1 January 2027. Commercial plans outside the covered programs are not bound at all.

comps.name: Clearinghouses
comps.purpose: Carries X12 278 requests and 277 status responses for payers without a FHIR surface. Still the majority path today.
outputs: 278 response, 277 status
comps.prod: CMS is applying enforcement discretion on the HIPAA X12 278 requirement where FHIR is implemented — but the pipe does not disappear.

comps.name: Exchange networks
comps.purpose: Reaches records from organisations you have no direct integration with, under a genuine treatment relationship. In the demo, this is how the missing TB screen is eventually found.
outputs: Outside encounters, documents and results
comps.prod: Requires clinical context and a permitted purpose. Not a route around the relationship requirement.
